events.title: Fortran 95 standardized
events.summary: In December 1997, the Fortran 95 standard was published — a refinement of Fortran 90 that made scientific code easier for compilers to optimize.
events.about: Fortran 95 tightened array features and added rules for functions with no side effects — helping compilers run scientific loops faster on supercomputers. Many legacy high-performance codes still target this dialect. Core numerical libraries assume Fortran 95 semantics.

narrative.whyChosen: Fortran 95 is the stable baseline many compilers and numerical libraries standardized on before later Fortran revisions.
narrative.whyImportant: Side-effect-free functions and improved array rules let supercomputer compilers squeeze more speed from weather, physics, and engineering simulations.
narrative.problemSolved: Fortran 90 left gaps that made it hard for compilers to safely optimize large numerical loops.
